title.narrative: UNDP Building Capacities for Trade Transnistria 2022-2026

description.narrative: Den föreslagna andra fasen av initiativet kommer att stödja utvecklingen av en möjliggörande miljö (inklusive kapacitetsutveckling och regleringsåtgärder) för samarbete över floden Dnestr och integration av exportörer, kommer att fortsätta att utöka tillgången för transnistriska företag (särskilt små och medelstora företag) till exportfrämjande mekanismer på högra sidan Dnestr, samt ge skräddarsytt stöd och bygga nödvändig kompetens som tar hänsyn till specifika behov hos nuvarande och framtida exportörer från regionen.

The proposed second phase of the initiative will support the development of the enabling environment (including capacity development and regulatory measures) for cross-river cooperation and integration of exporters, will continue expanding access of Transnistria enterprises (particularly SMEs) to export promotion mechanisms on the right bank, as well as provide tailored support and build necessary skills, taking into account specific needs of current and future exporters from the region.

The initiative will follow the general Project Objective as follows: Men and women on both banks of the Nistru River have improved livelihoods and living conditions, due to enhanced cross-river cooperation to access the opportunities offered by Moldova`s external trade arrangements, contributing to an environment of trust and cooperation across the post-conflict divide
To achieve this, the proposed intervention focuses on delivering the following specific outputs: Output 1. Improved cross-river exchange of information, knowledge and experience on the export promotion mechanisms on the right bank, and awareness-raising on the opportunities provided by external trade agreements. Output 2. Enhanced competitiveness and joint exports of business communities from both riverbanks with a particular focus on cluster and value chain development and export promotion. Output 3. Enhanced capacities for policy formulation leading to a conducive environment on both banks and reduction of barriers to trade and economic cooperation Output 4. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises across the Nistru river, in particular those led by women and benefitting vulnerable groups, are enabled to produce more competitive products

2022-2023 Under Output 1: Improved cross-river exchange of information, knowledge and experience on the export promotion mechanisms on the right bank, and awareness-raising on the opportunities provided by external trade agreements: 340 companies representatives have participated at various events related to the dissemination of information of foreign trade opportunities; masterclasses and B2B sessions were organized; significant results were achieved in enhancing capacities of social business and improvement of social entrepreneurship climate on the left bank.
Under Output 2: Enhanced competitiveness and joint exports of business communities from both riverbanks through improved companies exporting capacities and cluster and value chain development, the Export Accelerator initiative continued for 18 companies in enhancing their export capacities and knowledge. The project is committed to the establishment and development of up to six pilot cross-river business clusters and during 2023 the methodology and roadmap were agreed.
Under Output 3: Enhanced capacities for policy formulation leading to a conducive environment on both banks and reduction of barriers to trade and economic cooperation, the support was provided in the area of policy analysis and development for business enhancement and export promotion. This process involved deregulation, identifying barriers to export, understanding market trends and creating frameworks that encourage businesses to innovate and expand beyond domestic borders. AdTrade Project provided support to the Economic Council Secretariat to the Prime Minister of Moldova to deregulate and simplify SMEs activities.
Under Output 4: Expand the MSME sector in the Transnistrian region and security zone via support to new or emerging businesses, in particular women-led and with impact on the most vulnerable (migrants, young people including minorities representatives, elderly people) a series of targeted activities aimed at supporting new and emerging businesses, particularly those led by women, and impacting vulnerable groups were implemented. Key initiatives included mentoring and coaching for women and vulnerable groups, MSMEs support programs for new businesses, and the development of STEAM projects. The MSMEs contest attracted 223 applications from aspiring entrepreneurs and MSMEs across the region. Notably, 126 of these were submitted by women (56%), indicating a strong interest and participation from female entrepreneurs.
2024 Output 1: - Operations led to a sustained, cross-river knowledge hub: 340 MSME representatives trained on DCFTA provisions, customs and legal steps; 89 left-bank firms began tailored export strategies; 366 participants (200 women) joined workshops and study visits. - Seventeen business associations have upgraded their services: they now co-design simplified customs procedures, lobby to postpone ERP packaging rules, and streamline Lohn processing for textile imports. Business associations shifted from inward-looking membership groups to proactive trade facilitators. - Left-bank companies can now draft compliant export plans, navigate DCFTA and international trade agreements, adopt ESG and circular-economy models. - Early results: pilot sustainable projects, policy changes, strengthened BA networks and planned masterclasses, confirm the intervention is making a tangible difference.
Output 2: - Export Accelerator boosted business associations support role: 96 tailored mentoring sessions for six BAs led five of them to independently run export-promotion seminars reaching 53 MSMEs. - Twenty-five MSMEs now have customized export plans complete with strategy, market research and diversification targets (2 new markets, 10% export growth), capabilities they lacked pre-intervention. - BAs shifted from ad-hoc advisors to sustained export facilitators, continuing consultancy beyond project close-out and embedding export support into their core services. - Six cross-river pilot clusters (fruits, vegetables, beekeeping, tourism, textile, creative industries) formed via 75 fact-finding visits; Cluster Development Groups signed MoUs and now follow 3-year roadmaps to drive joint value-chain growth. - A Grant Program for micro-clusters selected 12 projects across both banks to fund modernization (equipment, infrastructure), training, digital marketing and trade missions, laying the groundwork for sustained competitiveness and export-driven growth.
Output 3: - Two deregulation packages drafted and approved, updating 66 laws and norms to streamline SME regulations and unlock potential savings of 194 million MDL. First Deregulation Package (50 laws; 183 million MDL saved) delivered: for example Health & Safety simplifications were possible by dropping adaptation and periodic computer-user exams; replaced doctors notes in travel sheets with a single control form. Second Deregulation Package (16 laws; 11 million MDL/year benefit) introduced: Digital shareholder relations and simpler voting procedures. Lower accreditation fees at MOLDAC and broader zone registration without extra authorization. - The project contributed to clearer, harmonized regulatory framework that smooths Nistru-River trade flows. Two BSOs mapped right and left-bank trade rules, pinpointed bureaucratic hurdles and delivered tailored compliance advice. BSOs moved from generic support to proactive, cross-bank facilitators; the Chamber of Commerce joined forces to resolve bottlenecks. - In close collaboration with the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, trade limits on subcontracted processing were lifted for at least three left-bank companies. Left-bank firms can now engage in raw-material processing and re-export finished goods freely. - Sixty-seven firms from both banks received one-on-one consultations on EPR rules and adapted their packaging, collection and reporting processes. Project contributed to alignment with regional environmental standards and reduced risk of non-compliance fines.
Output 4: - Start-up support was provided by 18 training sessions (13 on left bank, 5 on right bank). 80 individual and group sessions covering financial documentation, business processes, export strategies and HR, were provided. - MSME support programs for new businesses were implemented and: 23 enterprises (20 women-owned) received tailored support such as training, coaching and equipment grants; 127 jobs (83 for women) were retained and created, out of it 82 jobs on the right bank (54 women, 28 men) and 45 on the left bank (29 women, 16 men). Beneficiary financial contribution reached 37% (versus the required 20%), and the total program funding of $686,076 leveraged an additional $255,257 from beneficiaries.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
